mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.1% indicates an ultra-accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces discount rates for equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 9.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is above 9.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakness in consumer demand, which is a strong predictor of negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of low inflation (CPIAUCSL 12m growth rate below 2.0%) and low interest rates (FEDFUNDS below 0.5%), the S&P 500 tends to experience positive returns over the next 60 days as the economy remains stable and corporate profits are supported by cheap credit.
regime_hint: low inflation and low rates regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL 12m growth rate is below 2.0% and FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90.0 indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 90.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of weak housing starts (HOUST below 600) and slow GDP growth (GDPC1 growth rate below 1.0% annualized), the S&P 500 tends to underperform over the next 20 days due to reduced consumer confidence and business investment.
regime_hint: weak housing and slow GDP regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is below 600 and GDPC1 growth rate is below 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of industrial production (INDPRO above 95.0) indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is above 95.0.
